PullRequest.Title: Record CAPI X-Copilot-Service-Request-Id on chat telemetry events
PullRequest.Body:
Captures CAPI's X-Copilot-Service-Request-Id response header and threads it through chat fetch results, error paths, and websocket telemetry, so client-side telemetry events can be joined with CAPI's telemtry.

Also covers the retry-after-error and connectivity-test error paths, and adds a test asserting the id lands on chat response telemetry.

Scenarios.Scenario: HTTP chat completion over Responses, Messages, and chat-completions endpoints
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing CAPI HTTP request and response stream remain the critical path. The diff reads one response header while constructing request metadata and adds the resulting short string to existing completion/error telemetry; no new await or boundary is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the chat request and receive/stream the model response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing CAPI request per model attempt; retries remain governed by pre-existing retry logic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request and stream were performed; response metadata omitted X-Copilot-Service-Request-Id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network response is required before output can stream. The added header lookup happens after headers arrive and is bounded by the response-header count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue existing success, cancellation, or error telemetry with one additional request-id property
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing terminal telemetry events per attempt; the diff adds one short property and does not add events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same telemetry events were emitted without the service request id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous telemetry envelope construction gains a constant-size field; transport behavior and event count are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of HTTP model attempts, including concurrent subagent requests; each attempt carries one bounded request-id string. Stream length does not multiply the new header work in the endpoint processors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requests may execute concurrently as before; the diff adds no fan-out, limiter changes, or additional promises.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat POSTs are not served from the optional fetch cache on this path; the diff does not alter cache keys, misses, coalescing, or negative caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines only extract and propagate response metadata through existing objects and telemetry calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact response-header count and request-id length vary, but both are bounded and small relative to existing JSON/SSE processing and network latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added CPU, allocation, and telemetry bytes are constant per request and do not change critical-path boundary count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Network/server error connectivity check and transparent retry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After an existing eligible failure, configured delays and CAPI ping requests determine progress. The diff only reads the service request id from an already-returned non-2xx ping response and threads it through the existing retry telemetry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ping CAPI after an eligible error
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing ping per configured delay until success or exhaustion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same ping loop executed and recorded status/GitHub request id but not the CAPI service request id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pings and delays already block retry progress; the added header extraction does not add or delay another network request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry the failed chat request using the selected fetcher
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the same existing transparent retry selected by retry policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same retry was issued with less correlation metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The retry remains on the critical path; metadata propagation does not alter scheduling or concurrency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured connectivity-check attempt count and number of failed chat attempts; the new work is one bounded header lookup only on non-2xx ping responses plus constant metadata per retry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The ping loop is serialized by existing awaits, and the retry follows it; the diff does not increase concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connectivity pings and chat retries are uncached on this path; no cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff leaves delays, loop bounds, fetch calls, and retry conditions unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure prevalence varies, but the changed work remains constant per existing failed response.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No new I/O or fan-out is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reusable websocket chat connection and per-turn telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing websocket handshake opens the connection; each turn serializes and sends one request, then streams events. The new getter reads the handshake response header before existing connection and turn telemetry calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing handshake per reusable connection, not per streamed event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same handshake occurred and exposed the GitHub request id only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Handshake completion remains required before turns can send; the added bounded header lookup occurs after response headers are available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one serialized response.create message per chat turn and receive streamed websocket events
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing outbound websocket message per turn; incoming stream event count is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same websocket message and event stream were processed without service-id telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added id does not enter the websocket request payload or per-message event handler. It is added to existing sent/outcome telemetry only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue existing websocket connection, request-sent, outcome, close, or error telemetry with one extra property
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one connected event per connection and two events per completed turn (sent and outcome), with existing exceptional lifecycle events on failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event set was emitted without the service request id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No telemetry event is added. Header lookup and one short property are bounded and are not performed for every streamed websocket message.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Connections and turns, not token chunks. A reused connection performs a small bounded header lookup for existing lifecycle/turn telemetry calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection reuse and the existing single active-request/supersession behavior are unchanged; no burst or queue change is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The reusable websocket connection is the effective reuse mechanism. The id remains in existing response headers for the connection lifetime; no new cache or retained collection is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: message handlers show the getter is used for lifecycle/error and per-turn terminal telemetry, not the normal per-token stream path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of turns per connection varies, but each turn adds only constant lookup/serialization work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The metadata does not change websocket boundary count, payload, stream processing, or retained lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Inline/NES completions and generic SSE request-id processing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing completion HTTP request and SSE parsing drive latency. getRequestId now performs one additional lowercase header lookup; its case-insensitive fallback enumerates headers only when the direct lookup misses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send completion request and consume the SSE response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing request per completion attempt; request-id parsing occurs at processor initialization and may repeat for an initial metadata chunk until the first meaningful choice establishes created time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion request and SSE parse occurred, with getRequestId reading the existing request/experiment/deployment headers but not the service id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No boundary is added. Production Node/undici response headers are lowercased, making the new lookup direct when present; missing headers cause a scan over the small response-header set a bounded number of times.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy request-id properties into existing completion telemetry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing telemetry extension points per completion lifecycle; one additional string property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing telemetry copied the other request-id fields only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant object-property and payload growth; event count is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Completion request frequency and the small number of initialization chunks, not total generated token count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Completion requests retain existing cancellation and concurrency behavior; no extra async work or fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No response cache or coalescing behavior is changed. Header normalization by production Node/undici fetchers preserves direct lookup for lowercase names.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: SSEProcessor guards request-id refresh with created === 0, and production fetchers lowercase response header names.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Nonstandard test/custom IHeaders implementations can preserve casing, but fallback work remains proportional only to a small header set and bounded initialization reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The fallback does not become per-token repeated work and has bounded cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 21 changed files. Traced HTTP chat, retry/connectivity, websocket lifecycle/turns, generic SSE completions, header normalization, telemetry propagation, caching, and concurrency. The PR adds bounded metadata lookup/copy/serialization to existing boundaries and does not introduce additional network calls, fan-out, hot per-token scans, unbounded retention, or critical-path blocking.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
